answer_1.quote: The rise of LLMs has brought significant advancements to summarization tasks... We show that agent-based refinement improves factuality (+14.03), ROUGE (+2.05), and BERTScore (+0.13) on MovieSum, a movie script summarization dataset...

answer_2.quote: We assess the performance of our framework using several key evaluation metrics. ROUGE assesses n-gram overlap... BERTScore evaluates similarity... BARTScore measures the quality of summaries... Finally, we propose NARRATIVEFACTSCORE (NFS) as a novel metric to measure the factuality of the generated summaries.

answer_3.quote: LLM-as-a-Judge metrics have leveraged LLM to assess the factuality... We propose an Agent-as-a-Judge framework, using interpretable evaluation of summaries with a novel NARRATIVE-FACTSCORE... All components, including CKG extraction, summarization, fact decomposition, fact check, and agent-based fact refinement, use gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18.

answer_4.quote: Our metric demonstrates a statistically strong correlation with human evaluation, and a test for differences between human evaluation and our metric yielded statistically significant results... Thus, judging the factuality of such long narratives has therefore inevitably relied on costly human evaluations.
answer_4.guideline: Human raters scored the factuality of summary statements, providing a reference factuality score for correlation analysis.
